report.answer_text:
The captain, also called the master, has overall command of the ship and is responsible for its safe operation and the safety of its crew, passengers, and cargo. Officers carry out many day-to-day tasks, but the captain retains overall responsibility. (bls.gov)
| Main duty | What it involves |
|---|---|
| Navigate safely | Approve the voyage plan, oversee bridge watches, and adjust course or speed for weather, traffic, and other hazards. (onetonline.org) |
| Lead the crew | Give clear orders, assign duties through officers, and make sure the crew knows what to do in routine operations and emergencies. (bls.gov) |
| Keep the ship fit for the voyage | Oversee the ship’s condition and safety equipment, and ensure cargo is safely loaded and secured without compromising stability. (onetonline.org) |
| Prepare for and lead emergencies | Ensure drills are held and direct the response to fires, flooding, medical emergencies, or evacuation. (wwwcdn.imo.org) |
| Prevent pollution and ensure compliance | Implement the ship’s safety and pollution-prevention procedures, oversee required records, and ensure incidents are reported. (wwwcdn.imo.org) |
A key point: the captain has overriding authority to make decisions about safety and pollution prevention. For example, the captain can delay departure if conditions make sailing unsafe. (wwwcdn.imo.org)

quotes.text: The Company should clearly define an\l document the master's responsibility with regard to: .1 implementing the safety and environmental protection policy of the Company; .2 motivating the crew in the observation of that policy; .3 issuing appropriate orders and instructions in a clear and simple manner; .4 verifying that specified requirements are observed; and .5 reviewing the SMS and reporting its deficiencies to the shore based management.

The Company should establish in the SMS that the master has the overriding authority and the responsibility to make decisions with respect to safety and pollution prevention and to request the Company's assistance as may be necessary.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes back the captain's responsibility for implementing safety and environmental protection policy and for pollution prevention, but nothing in them mentions overseeing required records or ensuring incidents are reported; they only mention reporting SMS deficiencies to shore management.
pages.page_reason: The page's Section 5 states the Company should define the master's responsibility for implementing the safety and environmental protection policy, verifying requirements are observed, and reviewing the SMS and reporting deficiencies, and Section 9 requires non-conformities and accidents to be reported; however, it does not explicitly say the master oversees required records, so that part of the claim is only partly supported.
